reading: The Bank of England has maintained interest rates for the sixth consecutive time, yet indicated a probable increase if high energy prices persist.
This decision comes despite an uptick in the rate of inflation, with the main Bank rate remaining at 3.75%.
Global energy supplies have been disrupted by the US-Israel war with Iran, leading to a sharp increase in petrol and diesel costs.
Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey emphasized that prolonged volatility in energy prices would magnify its impact on inflation.
He stated that higher rates would then be necessary to ensure inflation returns to the 2% target.
The Bank now anticipates inflation will rise more than previously expected and forecasts a substantial increase in the January price cap for household gas and electricity.
Bailey noted the direct effect of elevated energy prices was evident, but officials are still evaluating their broader economic implications.
The Bank's main interest rate serves as a critical benchmark for lenders when determining borrowing and saving rates for individuals and businesses.
While financial markets have factored in potential rate hikes, Bailey cautioned that the global economic outlook remains "hugely unpredictable."
He specified that interest rates would only decrease with "an end of conflict in the Middle East... and energy prices coming really back to where they were before this conflict began."
On a positive note, the Bank reported that the UK economy proved "more resilient" than anticipated, revising its economic growth forecast for July to September to 0.4%.
Furthermore, food price inflation is projected to rise by 4% by year-end, a reduction from the earlier 6-7% forecast, as higher energy costs have not yet spilled over into other sectors.
Households typically face higher borrowing costs when the Bank rate rises, but can also benefit from more generous savings rates.
Consequently, numerous major lenders have already raised the cost of new fixed-rate mortgages in anticipation of a higher Bank rate.
The Bank also announced a halt to its "quantitative tightening" (QT) program, pausing the annual sale of government bonds.
Instead, it will divest smaller portions of its bond stockpile over eight years, a shift from its earlier practice of offloading bonds, which contributed to higher yields.
This change in strategy prompted an immediate market reaction, with yields on 30-year UK government bonds falling from 5.86% to 5.75% after the announcement.

vocabulary.definition: To keep something at the same level or standard, preventing it from decreasing or changing significantly.
Following one after another without interruption; in an unbroken sequence.
A small increase or slight improvement, often temporary, in a trend or measurement.
To make something appear larger, more intense, or more significant than it actually is; to amplify an effect.
Regards as probable or expects; to look forward to or prepare for something to happen.
Higher than the usual, normal, or expected level; increased in amount or degree.
The possible results or effects of an action or decision, which may not be immediately obvious.
A standard or point of reference against which things can be measured, compared, or assessed.
Included or considered something as a relevant element when making a calculation, plan, or assessment.
The tendency of something, especially prices or markets, to change rapidly and unpredictably, often for the worse.

entries.ja: 何かを同じ水準や基準に保ち、それが大幅に減少したり変化したりするのを防ぐこと。
entries.ko: 어떤 것을 동일한 수준이나 기준으로 유지하여 크게 감소하거나 변하지 않도록 하는 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 将某物保持在相同的水平或标准，阻止其显著下降或改变。
entries.es: Mantener algo en el mismo nivel o estándar, evitando que disminuya o cambie significativamente.
entries.pt-BR: Manter algo no mesmo nível ou padrão, evitando que diminua ou mude significativamente.

entries.ja: 中断することなく次々に続くこと。途切れない連続した順序で。
entries.ko: 중단 없이 하나 뒤에 다른 하나가 이어지는; 끊이지 않는 연속적인 순서로.
entries.zh-Hans: 不间断地一个接一个地发生；在不间断的序列中。
entries.es: Que sigue uno después de otro sin interrupción; en una secuencia ininterrumpida.
entries.pt-BR: Que segue um após o outro sem interrupção; em uma sequência ininterrupta.

entries.ja: 傾向や測定値において、しばしば一時的な小さな増加またはわずかな改善。
entries.ko: 추세나 측정치에서 종종 일시적인 작은 증가나 약간의 개선.
entries.zh-Hans: 趋势或测量中，通常是暂时的，小幅度的增长或轻微的改善。
entries.es: Un pequeño aumento o ligera mejora, a menudo temporal, en una tendencia o medición.
entries.pt-BR: Um pequeno aumento ou leve melhoria, muitas vezes temporária, em uma tendência ou medição.

entries.ja: 何かを実際よりも大きく、より強烈に、またはより重要に見せること。効果を増幅すること。
entries.ko: 어떤 것을 실제보다 더 크게, 더 강렬하게, 또는 더 중요하게 보이게 하는 것; 효과를 증폭시키는 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 使某物看起来比实际更大、更强烈或更重要；放大某种效应。
entries.es: Hacer que algo parezca más grande, más intenso o más significativo de lo que realmente es; amplificar un efecto.
entries.pt-BR: Fazer algo parecer maior, mais intenso ou mais significativo do que realmente é; amplificar um efeito.

entries.ja: ある事柄が起こる可能性が高いと見なすこと、または予期すること。何かが起こるのを楽しみにしたり、それに備えたりすること。
entries.ko: 어떤 일이 일어날 것이라고 생각하거나 기대하는 것; 어떤 일이 일어나기를 고대하거나 준비하는 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 认为某事很可能发生或预期会发生；期待或为某事的发生做准备。
entries.es: Considerar algo probable o esperarlo; anhelar que algo suceda o prepararse para ello.
entries.pt-BR: Considerar como provável ou esperar; aguardar ou preparar-se para que algo aconteça.

entries.ja: 通常の、標準的な、または予想されるレベルよりも高いこと。量や程度が増加していること。
entries.ko: 평소, 정상 또는 예상 수준보다 더 높은; 양이나 정도가 증가한.
entries.zh-Hans: 高于通常、正常或预期水平；数量或程度有所增加。
entries.es: Más alto que el nivel habitual, normal o esperado; aumentado en cantidad o grado.
entries.pt-BR: Mais alto do que o nível usual, normal ou esperado; aumentado em quantidade ou grau.

entries.ja: 行動や決定の考えられる結果や影響で、すぐには明らかではないかもしれないもの。
entries.ko: 행동이나 결정의 가능한 결과나 영향으로, 즉시 명확하지 않을 수 있는 것들.
entries.zh-Hans: 某种行动或决定可能产生的结果或影响，这些结果或影响可能不会立即显现。
entries.es: Los posibles resultados o efectos de una acción o decisión, que pueden no ser inmediatamente obvios.
entries.pt-BR: Os possíveis resultados ou efeitos de uma ação ou decisão, que podem não ser inmediatamente obvios.

entries.ja: 物事を測定、比較、評価するための基準となる標準や参照点。
entries.ko: 어떤 것을 측정하거나 비교, 평가할 수 있는 기준 또는 참고점.
entries.zh-Hans: 一个标准或参考点，可以用来衡量、比较或评估事物。
entries.es: Un estándar o punto de referencia contra el cual las cosas pueden ser medidas, comparadas o evaluadas.
entries.pt-BR: Um padrão ou ponto de referência contra o qual as coisas podem ser medidas, comparadas ou avaliadas.

entries.ja: 計算、計画、または評価を行う際に、関連する要素として何かを含めたり考慮に入れたりすること。
entries.ko: 계산, 계획 또는 평가를 할 때, 어떤 것을 관련 요소로 포함하거나 고려한.
entries.zh-Hans: 在进行计算、计划或评估时，将某事作为一个相关因素包括或考虑在内。
entries.es: Incluir o considerar algo como un elemento relevante al hacer un cálculo, plan o evaluación.
entries.pt-BR: Incluir ou considerar algo como um elemento relevante ao fazer um cálculo, plano ou avaliação.

entries.ja: 特に価格や市場が、しばしば悪い方向へ急速かつ予測不能に変化する傾向。
entries.ko: 특히 가격이나 시장이 빠르고 예측 불가능하게, 종종 나쁜 방향으로 변하는 경향.
entries.zh-Hans: 某事物，特别是价格或市场，快速且不可预测地变化（通常是恶化）的趋势。
entries.es: La tendencia de algo, especialmente los precios o los mercados, a cambiar rápida e impredeciblemente, a menudo para peor.
entries.pt-BR: A tendência de algo, especialmente preços ou mercados, a cambiar rápida e imprevisiblemente, a menudo para peor.
